name: Terraces / High Camp
description:
Leader: Ian Wallace

Description:
A club classic walk, up Palm Creek (St ​Margaret's Creek system) to the Terraces, Ultima Falls, Garden Wall, and High Camp.

A creek-based walk with many waterfalls, one of the most scenic creeks in the region (and the state) and one of the local gems.

The club had been bushwalking St Margaret's Creek system since 1966 ! Pioneers of the great local bushwalks that bushwalkers enjoy today.

Type of walk:
Full day hike, creek based and cross country, rough terrain. Rock hopping, boulder scrambles, rockface traverses, scrub and vines, uneven footing, slippery rocks, steep climbs. On way out, includes a stop at the at the Rockslides for a swim, then the walk back to the cars. And most important, ice creams at the roadhouse on the way home to finish the day off. A good day out for our adventurous bushwalkers.

Here is a link to some pictures on our Facebook Group, to give you an idea of what the terrain is like and the walk in general - https://www.facebook.com/townsvillebushwalkingclub/photos/pcb.694167834837167/694166344837316

Distance: 11 km, elevation change 300m 

Cost: non-members $5 fee.

What you need:
carry water (minimum 2 lt), refill from creek as required (treat / filter your water refill) . Lunch,  snacks / energy food, electrolytes, hat, sunscreen, insect repellent, enclosed sturdy footwear. Recommend long sleeve clothing / gaiters to avoid scratches. Some members also wear fingerless gloves.
 
Timing and meet:
Meet 07:30 at the Alligator Creek Caltex roadhouse - junction Bentley Drive / Bruce Hwy, Alligator Creek. We will be carpooling from there. 

Estimated Completion: back at cars around 5 pm.

Register Here -  
Walk Full - Thank you everyone

name: Lower Little Crystal Creek Falls
description:
Leader: Luen Warneke.

Description:
The walk is steep, off-track, and uneven underfoot. 
The hike starts by steeply descending into the Little Crystal Valley through bushland. Once we reach the creek, we will enjoy a scenic waterfall and swim in the large pool at its base. The return hike out will get your heart beating and make you sweaty. 

Type of walk:

Half-day hike, cross country over rough terrain. Boulder scrambles, uneven footing, slippery rocks, steep climbs. A great experience for those who are fit and are just getting into bushwalking.

Here is a link to the Townsville Bush Walking Club's Facebook Group- the link here will give you an idea of what the terrain for this particular hike will be like:
https://www.facebook.com/townsvillebushwalkingclub/photos/pcb.643252566595361/643251446595473/

Cost: non-members $5 fee.

What you need: 
carry water (minimum 2 lt), refill from creek as required (treat / filter your water refill) . Lunch,  snacks / energy food, electrolytes, hat, sunscreen, insect repellent, enclosed sturdy footwear. Recommend long sleeve clothing / gaiters to avoid scratches. Some members also wear fingerless gloves.

Timing and meet – Meet 06:30 at Deeragun BP and can car pool from there
 
Estimated Completion: back at cars around 11 am - just in time for lunch.

Group size:
Group size limited to 12 people. The walk leader reserves the right to refuse permission to join the walk if they think it would be unsuitable for you. We would rate this walk as an easy to medium half-day walk

name: Paradise Beach & Castle Rock
description:
The next Club walk will be held on 15 May to Paradise Beach & Castle Rock. 
Wilfred Karnoll is the leader  

The walk commences at the end of Cape Cleveland Road and follows a rough, but well-defined track around the perimeter of AIMS and hits the northern end of the AIMS beach.  From there it's up and over the saddle, and through the coastal forest to the Little Beach.  Again, this is a marked track and ascends about 60 m at the most.  Enjoy the views once you get to the saddle of Little Beach and beyond.  

The shoreline has changed so much at Little Beach since we first went there in the early 2010s after the big monsoonal rains about 4 years ago.  It's still a beautiful little spot though.  About half way along the beach a second creek flows down to it and you'll make your way up the creek then cross over to the northern bank and follow the track all the way to the second saddle.  There is a great lookout to your right , but it's a little bit off the beaten track.  The descent to Paradise Beach is straight forward and follows a track.  

Castle Rock is at the northern end of the beach, you will either enjoy a long stroll along the beach followed by a very steep ascent to the Rock or cut inland in order to take a more gradual ascent to Castle Rock.  Don't worry you'll still get the steep scramble at the end no matter which way you go!  Your heart rate will be ever so elevated by the time you hit the high point and see spectacular views to the north and south of you.  Enjoy your lunch at the summit and prepare yourself for the journey back to the cars.  The return journey largely follows the same route, but there are often a couple of alternative routes to use to leave Castle Rock.  Whatever you do, don't be tempted if the word "Balancing" is used.  That's another story though.  

What do you bring?  Well, it's the usual requirements for a day walk.  Hat, sunscreen and insect repellent.  Long sleeved shirts, long trousers or shorts with gaiters will protect you from the sun and scratches.  Morning tea, lunch and afternoon tea, plus sundry snacks to sustain you throughout the day.  First aid kit and a snake bandage are always essentials.  Camera.  Togs & towel to have a swim at Paradise Beach.  

Water.  I would suggest 3 - 4 L as it will be a long walk and although there has been recent rain we have never assumed the water supply is reliable.

Please call Wilfred to nominate for the walk or email Contact info@townsvillebushwalkingclub.    Wilfred reserves the right to refuse permission to join the walk if he thinks it would be unsuitable for you.  We would rate this walk as an easy to medium, yet long day walk.
